source.text: Ὅθεν, ἀδελφοὶ ἅγιοι, κλήσεως ἐπουρανίου μέτοχοι, κατανοήσατε τὸν ἀπόστολον καὶ ἀρχιερέα τῆς ὁμολογίας ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν, πιστὸν ὄντα τῷ ποιήσαντι αὐτὸν ὡς καὶ Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore, brothers holy, of calling heavenly partakers, consider the apostle and high priest of the confession of us, Jesus, \v 2 faithful being to the [one] having appointed him, as also Moses in the house of him.

en.L: Therefore, holy {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, partakers of a heavenly calling, consider the apostle and high priest of our confession, Jesus, \v 2 being faithful to the [one] who appointed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, as Moses also [was] in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} house.
en.B: So then, holy {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, partners in a heavenly calling, turn your minds to Jesus, the apostle and high priest of the confession we make. \v 2 He was faithful to God, who appointed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, as Moses too was faithful in God's house.
en.R: So, holy {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, God has called you from heaven, and you share in that call together. Think carefully about Jesus. God sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to us, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the high priest of the faith we confess. \v 2 He was faithful to God, who gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} this work, just as Moses was faithful in God's house, among God's people.

es.L: Por tanto, hermanos santos, partícipes de un llamamiento celestial, {{plural_you:consideren|considerad}} al apóstol y sumo sacerdote de nuestra confesión, Jesús, \v 2 que es fiel al que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} designó, como también Moisés [lo fue] en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} casa.
es.B: Así pues, hermanos santos, compañeros en un llamamiento celestial, {{plural_you:fijen|fijad}} la mente en Jesús, el apóstol y sumo sacerdote de la confesión que hacemos. \v 2 Él fue fiel a Dios, que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} designó, como también Moisés fue fiel en la casa de Dios.
es.R: Así que, hermanos santos, Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} ha llamado desde el cielo, y {{plural_you:comparten|compartís}} juntos ese llamado. {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} bien en Jesús. Dios nos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} envió, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es el sumo sacerdote de la fe que confesamos. \v 2 Él fue fiel a Dios, que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dio esta tarea, así como Moisés fue fiel en la casa de Dios, entre el pueblo de Dios.

fr.L: Par conséquent, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} saints, participants d’un appel céleste, considérez l’apôtre et grand prêtre de notre confession, Jésus, \v 2 étant fidèle à celui qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a établi, comme Moïse aussi [l’était] dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} maison.
fr.B: Ainsi donc, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} saints, vous qui êtes associés à un appel céleste, fixez votre attention sur Jésus, l’apôtre et le grand prêtre de la confession que nous faisons. \v 2 Il a été fidèle à Dieu, qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a établi, comme Moïse, lui aussi, a été fidèle dans la maison de Dieu.
fr.R: Alors, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} saints, Dieu vous a appelés du ciel, et vous avez part ensemble à cet appel. Pensez bien à Jésus. Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a envoyé vers nous, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est le grand prêtre de la foi que nous proclamons. \v 2 Il a été fidèle à Dieu, qui {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a confié cette tâche, comme Moïse a été fidèle dans la maison de Dieu, au milieu du peuple de Dieu.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo, ndugu watakatifu, washiriki wa wito wa mbinguni, mtafakarini mtume na kuhani mkuu wa ukiri wetu, Yesu, \v 2 aliye mwaminifu kwa [yule] aliyemweka, kama Musa naye [alivyokuwa] katika nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Basi, ndugu watakatifu, mnaoshiriki wito wa mbinguni, elekezeni mawazo yenu kwa Yesu, mtume na kuhani mkuu wa ukiri tunaoutamka. \v 2 Alikuwa mwaminifu kwa Mungu aliyemweka, kama Musa naye alivyokuwa mwaminifu katika nyumba ya Mungu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo, ndugu watakatifu, Mungu amewaita kutoka mbinguni, nanyi mnashiriki wito huo pamoja. Mfikirieni Yesu kwa makini. Mungu alimtuma kwetu, na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni kuhani mkuu wa imani tunayoikiri. \v 2 Alikuwa mwaminifu kwa Mungu aliyempa kazi hii, kama Musa alivyokuwa mwaminifu katika nyumba ya Mungu, yaani kati ya watu wa Mungu.

decisions.choice: apostle: one sent out with authority to speak for the one who sends him
decisions.reason: This is the only place in the New Testament where Jesus is called an apostle. The author has said that God spoke to us in the Son (1:2) and that the message was first spoken through the Lord (2:3). Jesus is the one God sent to speak for him, and the high priest who speaks for us to God; the two titles come together in one person.

decisions.choice: a heavenly calling: a call that comes from heaven and leads there
alternatives: a call to go to heaven only
decisions.reason: The adjective describes where the call comes from and where it leads: God calls from heaven, where Christ now is (1:3; 4:14), and calls people to share his glory (2:10; 12:22-24).

decisions.choice: high priest of our confession: the high priest whom our confession is about
alternatives: the high priest who leads our confession
decisions.reason: ὁμολογία is what believers openly declare about Jesus (4:14; 10:23). The genitive says that Jesus, as apostle and high priest, is the content of what they confess.

decisions.choice: the one who appointed him: God, who appointed Jesus to his office
alternatives: the one who made him (created him)
decisions.reason: ποιέω usually means "make", but it is also used of appointing someone to a task: "he appointed twelve" (Mark 3:14), and the Greek of 1 Samuel 12:6 says the Lord "made" Moses and Aaron, meaning he appointed them. The author is speaking of Jesus' appointment as high priest (5:5), not of his origin.

decisions.choice: Numbers 12:7
decisions.reason: God says of Moses, "He is faithful in all my house" (Numbers 12:7). "His house" is therefore God's house, as in the verse quoted.

decisions.choice: house: God's household, his people, with the picture of a building
alternatives: a building only (the tabernacle or temple)
decisions.reason: οἶκος means a building and also the household that lives in it, as in "the house of Israel". In Numbers 12:7 it is God's people, whom Moses served. The author uses both senses: a house has a builder (3:3-4), and "we are his house" (3:6). Keeping the one word "house" through 3:2-6 lets the reader follow the argument.

decisions.choice: in his house (without "all")
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "in his house". Many manuscripts read "in all his house", with ὅλῳ, as 3:5 and Numbers 12:7 have it; the word may have been added to match those verses. From general knowledge, early witnesses that leave it out include the papyri P13 and P46 and Codex Vaticanus, while Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Alexandrinus and most later manuscripts include it. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus. The meaning is hardly affected.

decisions.choice: faithful to God, who appointed him; God's house
alternatives: faithful to the one who appointed him; his house
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God, who is the one who appointed Jesus and whose house it is (Numbers 12:7).

decisions.choice: partners in a heavenly calling
decisions.reason: The same word is used in 1:9 for the king's companions and in 3:14 for being Christ's partners; "partners" keeps the three together at Balanced.

decisions.choice: God sent him to us; in God's house, among God's people
decisions.reason: Readable explains "apostle" as one God sent, and says that the house is God's people, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so, as in Romans and Colossians, there is no gender span on it in Hebrews. The whole church is addressed.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: Hebrews speaks to its readers in the plural. Every plural "you", its possessive and every verb addressed to the readers is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain).

decisions.choice: ndugu, no gender span; deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns
decisions.reason: Swahili "ndugu" means a brother or sister, a relative or a fellow believer, so it already includes the women of the church, and a male-only alternative would change the meaning. Swahili marks most pronouns for God or Christ inside the verb ("aliyemweka", "alimtuma"), where they cannot be capitalized, so the deity_pronoun setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives ("yeye", "nyumba yake"), and the Swahili of Hebrews has fewer spans than the English.

decisions.choice: kuhani mkuu; ukiri (L, B), imani tunayoikiri (R)
decisions.reason: "kuhani mkuu" is the high priest throughout Hebrews. The confession is the faith believers openly declare about Jesus (m3): "ukiri", from "kukiri" (to acknowledge openly), at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "imani tunayoikiri" (the faith we confess), as the English Readable does, and 4:14 does the same. "maungamo" would suggest confessing sins.

decisions.choice: grand prêtre; confession (L, B), la foi que nous proclamons (R); {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}
decisions.reason: The French terms settled for the whole of Hebrews. "grand prêtre" is the plain modern word for the high priest; "souverain sacrificateur" is the older Protestant term. The confession is what believers openly declare about Jesus (m3): "confession" at Literal and Balanced, and at Readable "la foi que nous proclamons", as the English Readable says "the faith we confess"; 4:14 does the same. The readers are men and women, so "frères et sœurs" is the default and the traditional "frères" the alternative, as in the English.

decisions.choice: participants (L); associés (B)
decisions.reason: The same word returns in 3:14 ("partners of Christ"). Literal says "participants" in both places; Balanced says "associés", which keeps the sense of sharing in something together without the business tone of "partenaires". Readable says "vous avez part ensemble" here and "associés" in 3:14.

source.text: πλείονος γὰρ οὗτος δόξης παρὰ Μωϋσῆν ἠξίωται καθ’ ὅσον πλείονα τιμὴν ἔχει τοῦ οἴκου ὁ κατασκευάσας αὐτόν·

records.literal_gloss: Of more for this [one] glory than Moses has been counted worthy, by as much as more honor has of the house the [one] having built it;

en.L: For this [one] has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses, by as much as the [one] who built it has more honor than the house;
en.B: For Jesus has been judged worthy of more glory than Moses, as surely as the builder of a house is given more honor than the building.
en.R: Jesus deserves more glory than Moses, in the same way that the person who builds a house deserves more honor than the house.

es.L: Porque este ha sido considerado digno de más gloria que Moisés, tanto más cuanto el que la construyó tiene más honra que la casa;
es.B: Porque Jesús ha sido juzgado digno de más gloria que Moisés, así como quien construye una casa recibe más honra que el edificio.
es.R: Jesús merece más gloria que Moisés, de la misma manera que la persona que construye una casa merece más honra que la casa.

fr.L: Car celui-ci a été jugé digne d’une gloire plus grande que Moïse, d’autant que celui qui l’a construite a plus d’honneur que la maison ;
fr.B: Car Jésus a été jugé digne de plus de gloire que Moïse, de même que celui qui bâtit une maison reçoit plus d’honneur que la maison elle-même.
fr.R: Jésus mérite plus de gloire que Moïse, tout comme celui qui construit une maison mérite plus d’honneur que la maison.

sw.L: Kwa maana huyu amehesabiwa kustahili utukufu zaidi kuliko Musa, kwa kiasi kile ambacho mwenye kuijenga ana heshima zaidi kuliko nyumba;
sw.B: Kwa maana Yesu amehesabiwa kustahili utukufu zaidi kuliko Musa, kama vile mjenzi wa nyumba anavyopewa heshima zaidi kuliko jengo lenyewe.
sw.R: Yesu anastahili utukufu zaidi kuliko Musa, kama vile mtu anayejenga nyumba anavyostahili heshima zaidi kuliko nyumba yenyewe.

decisions.choice: the builder outranks the house: Moses belongs to the house, Jesus stands with its builder
alternatives: the author directly calls Jesus the builder of the house
decisions.reason: The comparison is drawn from ordinary life: whoever builds a house is honored above it. Moses was part of God's household, faithful within it (3:5). Jesus' honor is like the builder's. Verse 4 names God as the builder of everything; the author has also said that through the Son God made the ages (1:2, 1:10), so he may mean that Jesus shares in the building, but he does not say so outright.

decisions.choice: has been counted worthy: by God
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the one who judges unnamed; in the letter it is God who has given the Son his honor (1:3-4; 2:9).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, whom "this one" refers to (3:1).

source.text: πᾶς γὰρ οἶκος κατασκευάζεται ὑπό τινος, ὁ δὲ πάντα κατασκευάσας θεός.

records.literal_gloss: Every for house is built by someone, the [one] but all [things] having built [is] God.

en.L: For every house is built by someone, but the [one] who built all things [is] God.
en.B: Every house, after all, has someone who built it; and the one who built everything is God.
en.R: Someone builds every house. And God is the one who built everything there is.

es.L: Porque toda casa es construida por alguien, pero el que construyó todas las cosas [es] Dios.
es.B: Después de todo, toda casa tiene a alguien que la construyó; y el que lo construyó todo es Dios.
es.R: Alguien construye cada casa. Y Dios es quien construyó todo lo que existe.

fr.L: Car toute maison est construite par quelqu’un, mais celui qui a construit toutes [choses est] Dieu.
fr.B: Toute maison, en effet, a quelqu’un qui l’a construite ; et celui qui a tout construit, c’est Dieu.
fr.R: Toute maison est construite par quelqu’un. Et c’est Dieu qui a construit tout ce qui existe.

sw.L: Kwa maana kila nyumba hujengwa na mtu fulani, lakini aliyejenga kila kitu [ni] Mungu.
sw.B: Kila nyumba, hata hivyo, ina mtu aliyeijenga; na aliyejenga kila kitu ni Mungu.
sw.R: Kila nyumba hujengwa na mtu fulani. Na Mungu ndiye aliyejenga kila kitu kilichopo.

decisions.choice: God built everything, so the house in which Moses served and over which the Son is set is God's
decisions.reason: The verse grounds the comparison in 3:3: behind every house is a builder, and behind all things is God. The house of 3:2-6 is his, and Moses and the Son are each faithful to him.

source.text: καὶ Μωϋσῆς μὲν πιστὸς ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ ὡς θεράπων εἰς μαρτύριον τῶν λαληθησομένων, Χριστὸς δὲ ὡς υἱὸς ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ· ὅς οἶκός ἐσμεν ἡμεῖς, ἐὰν τὴν παρρησίαν καὶ τὸ καύχημα τῆς ἐλπίδος κατάσχωμεν.

records.literal_gloss: And Moses on one hand [was] faithful in whole the house of him as servant for testimony of the [things] going to be spoken, \v 6 Christ but as son over the house of him; whose house are we, if the boldness and the boast of the hope we hold fast.

en.L: And Moses [was] faithful in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} house as a servant, for a testimony of the things that would be spoken, \v 6 but {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} as Son over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} house; whose house we are, if we hold fast the boldness and the boast of the hope.
en.B: Moses was faithful in all God's house as a servant, bearing witness to what God would speak in days to come. \v 6 But {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is faithful as the Son, set over God's house. And we are that house, if we keep hold of our confidence and of the hope we take pride in.
en.R: Moses was faithful in all of God's house as a servant there, and his work pointed ahead to what God would say later. \v 6 But {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is faithful as the Son, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is in charge of God's house. And we are God's house, if we keep holding on to our confidence and to the hope we are proud of.

es.L: Y Moisés [fue] fiel en toda {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} casa como servidor, para testimonio de las cosas que se iban a decir, \v 6 pero {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, como Hijo sobre {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} casa; cuya casa somos nosotros, si retenemos firme la franqueza y el orgullo de la esperanza.
es.B: Moisés fue fiel en toda la casa de Dios como servidor, y dio testimonio de lo que Dios diría en días venideros. \v 6 Pero {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} es fiel como el Hijo, puesto al frente de la casa de Dios. Y nosotros somos esa casa, si seguimos aferrados a nuestra confianza y a la esperanza de la que nos gloriamos.
es.R: Moisés fue fiel en toda la casa de Dios como servidor en ella, y su trabajo señalaba hacia lo que Dios diría más adelante. \v 6 Pero {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} es fiel como el Hijo, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} está a cargo de la casa de Dios. Y nosotros somos la casa de Dios, si no soltamos nuestra confianza ni la esperanza que nos llena de orgullo.

fr.L: Et Moïse [était] fidèle dans toute {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} maison en tant que serviteur, en témoignage des choses qui allaient être dites, \v 6 mais {{christos:Christ|Messie}} comme Fils sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} maison ; maison que nous sommes, nous, si nous retenons fermement la hardiesse et la fierté de l’espérance.
fr.B: Moïse a été fidèle dans toute la maison de Dieu comme serviteur, rendant témoignage à ce que Dieu allait dire dans les temps à venir. \v 6 Mais le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est fidèle comme Fils, placé à la tête de la maison de Dieu. Et cette maison, c’est nous, si nous gardons fermement notre assurance et l’espérance dont nous sommes fiers.
fr.R: Moïse a été fidèle dans toute la maison de Dieu, comme serviteur, et son travail annonçait ce que Dieu dirait plus tard. \v 6 Mais le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est fidèle comme Fils, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a la charge de la maison de Dieu. Et la maison de Dieu, c’est nous, si nous continuons à garder notre assurance et l’espérance dont nous sommes fiers.

sw.L: Na Musa [alikuwa] mwaminifu katika nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yote akiwa mtumishi, kwa ushuhuda wa mambo ambayo yangesemwa, \v 6 lakini {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} akiwa Mwana juu ya nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}; ambaye sisi tu nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, ikiwa tunashikilia kwa uthabiti ujasiri na fahari ya tumaini.
sw.B: Musa alikuwa mwaminifu katika nyumba yote ya Mungu akiwa mtumishi, akishuhudia yale ambayo Mungu angesema siku za baadaye. \v 6 Lakini {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ni mwaminifu akiwa Mwana, aliyewekwa juu ya nyumba ya Mungu. Na sisi ndio nyumba hiyo, ikiwa tunaendelea kushikilia ujasiri wetu na tumaini tunalojivunia.
sw.R: Musa alikuwa mwaminifu katika nyumba yote ya Mungu akiwa mtumishi humo, na kazi yake ilielekeza kwenye yale ambayo Mungu angesema baadaye. \v 6 Lakini {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ni mwaminifu akiwa Mwana, na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye msimamizi wa nyumba ya Mungu. Nasi ni nyumba ya Mungu, ikiwa tunaendelea kushikilia ujasiri wetu na tumaini tunalojivunia.

decisions.choice: servant: an honored attendant, trusted with his master's affairs
decisions.reason: θεράπων is not the ordinary word for a slave. It is the word the Greek of Numbers 12:7 uses when God calls Moses "my servant" (also Exodus 14:31), a trusted attendant in God's house. The author honors Moses and still ranks him below the Son: a servant in the house, a son over it.

decisions.choice: Numbers 12:7
decisions.reason: "Faithful in all his house" repeats God's words about Moses in Numbers 12:7.

decisions.choice: bearing witness to what God would say later: Moses' service pointed ahead to the fuller word spoken in the Son
alternatives: to testify to the things Moses himself would be told to say (the law)
decisions.reason: The future participle looks ahead. In this letter God spoke in the past through the prophets and has now spoken in a Son (1:1-2); the law and the tabernacle were a shadow of what was to come (8:5; 10:1). The phrase may simply mean the words God would speak to Moses for the people, but the contrast with the Son in the next words favors the forward look.

decisions.choice: the Son is over God's house, where Moses was in it
decisions.reason: "His house" most naturally means God's house, as in 3:2 and 3:5, and the contrast is between "in" and "over". Because the Son is heir of all things (1:2), the house can also be called his, but the author's point is his position over it.

decisions.choice: we are that house: God's people now are the household of God
decisions.reason: The house in which Moses served was Israel; the author tells the readers that they are now that household, under the Son.

decisions.choice: confidence and the hope we boast in
alternatives: the boast that our hope gives
decisions.reason: παρρησία is the open confidence of people who belong and may speak freely (4:16; 10:19, 10:35). καύχημα of the hope is the pride and open joy believers take in what they hope for, not self-praise.

decisions.choice: the condition: we are God's house if we hold on
decisions.reason: The warning that runs through the letter is that belonging shows itself in holding firm to the end (3:14; 6:11; 10:23, 10:35-39).

decisions.choice: if we hold fast the boldness and the boast of the hope
alternatives: ... the boast of the hope firm to the end
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add μέχρι τέλους βεβαίαν ("firm to the end"), the words of 3:14, which are probably carried over from there. From general knowledge, the papyri P13 and P46 and Codex Vaticanus lack them, while Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Alexandrinus and most later manuscripts have them. The SBLGNT leaves them out. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: which house we are
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads ὅς, a relative agreeing with "house". Some manuscripts read οὗ ("whose"), so that the house is Christ's or God's. From general knowledge, P46 is among them. The sense is close either way. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (Literal); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: Son, capitalized
decisions.reason: Here the word is the title of Christ (1:2, 1:5, 1:8), set against Moses the servant, so it is capitalized at every level.

decisions.choice: God's house; is faithful as the Son, set over God's house
alternatives: his house; Christ as Son over his house
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the verb of 3:6a to be carried over from 3:5 ("faithful"). Balanced and Readable supply it and name God as the owner of the house.

decisions.choice: confidence
decisions.reason: Literal says "boldness"; Balanced and Readable say "confidence", the book-wide rendering of this word.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} (L); {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no article here, and Literal leaves it out, as the English Literal does. Balanced and Readable use the title with its article, "el Mesías", as a Spanish reader expects.

decisions.choice: servidor
decisions.reason: The meaning decision describes an honored attendant trusted with his master's affairs. "Siervo" can suggest a serf or a slave, and "criado" a domestic hired hand; "servidor" is one who serves without either overtone.

decisions.choice: franqueza (L); confianza (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "franqueza", the open, unafraid speech the word first meant. Balanced and Readable say "confianza", the sense the English gives it here; the same pair is used through Hebrews (4:16, 10:19, 10:35).

decisions.choice: mtumishi (servant)
decisions.reason: The Greek word here is not the one rendered "mtumwa" (slave) elsewhere in the New Testament; it is the honored attendant of Numbers 12:7 (m1), trusted with his master's house, so "mtumishi", as the English has "servant".

decisions.choice: ujasiri; fahari ya tumaini (L), tumaini tunalojivunia (B, R)
decisions.reason: "ujasiri" is the Hebrews word for this boldness and confidence (also 4:16; 10:19, 10:35): the freedom of people who are not ashamed or afraid. Literal keeps the noun "fahari" (pride, boast); Balanced and Readable say "the hope we take pride in" with the verb "kujivunia".

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messie}} (L); le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} (B, R)
alternatives: Christ without the article at every level
decisions.reason: Title setting, as in the English. Literal follows the Greek, which has no article; Balanced and Readable put the article outside the span, so that both "le Christ" and "le Messie" read naturally.

decisions.choice: hardiesse (L); assurance (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide French for this word: "hardiesse" at Literal keeps the sense of boldness, and "assurance" at Balanced and Readable is the confidence of people who belong (m6), as in 4:16 and 10:19.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore, as says the Spirit the Holy: Today if the voice of him you hear, \v 8 not harden the hearts of you as in the rebellion, according to the day of the testing in the wilderness, \v 9 where tested the fathers of you in examination and saw the works of me \v 10 forty years; therefore I was angry with the generation this and said: Always they go astray in the heart; they but not knew the ways of me;

en.L: Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: "Today, if you hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, \v 8 do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion, on the day of the testing in the wilderness, \v 9 where your fathers tested [{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}] by examining [{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}] and saw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} works \v 10 forty years. Therefore I was angry with this generation and said, 'They always go astray in [their] heart, and they did not know {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ways';
en.B: So, as the Holy Spirit says, "Today, if you hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, \v 8 do not harden your hearts as happened in the rebellion, on that day of testing in the wilderness, \v 9 where your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} put {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to the test and tried {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and saw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} works \v 10 for forty years. That is why I was angry with this generation, and I said, 'Their hearts are forever wandering; they have never come to know {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ways.'
en.R: That is why the Holy Spirit says, "Today, if you hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, \v 8 do not make your hearts hard, as the people did when they rebelled. That was the day they tested {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the wilderness. \v 9 There your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} put {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to the test, and they saw what I did \v 10 for forty years. So I was angry with this generation. I said, 'Their hearts are always wandering away. They have never learned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ways.'

Por eso me enojé con esta generación y dije: “Siempre se extravían en [su] corazón, y ellos no conocieron {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} caminos”;

Fue el día en que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pusieron a prueba en el desierto. \v 9 Allí {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} {{gender:antepasados|padres}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} desafiaron, y vieron lo que hice \v 10 durante cuarenta años. Por eso me enojé con esta generación. Dije: “Su corazón siempre anda extraviado. Nunca han aprendido {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} caminos”.

C’est pourquoi j’ai été irrité contre cette génération et j’ai dit : “Toujours ils s’égarent dans [leur] cœur, et ils n’ont pas connu {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} voies” ;
fr.B: Ainsi, comme le dit l’Esprit Saint : « Aujourd’hui, si vous entendez {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} voix, \v 8 n’endurcissez pas vos cœurs comme ce fut le cas lors de la rébellion, en ce jour d’épreuve au désert, \v 9 où vos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont mis à l’épreuve et {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont soumis à l’examen, et ont vu {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} œuvres \v 10 pendant quarante ans. fr.R: C’est pourquoi l’Esprit Saint dit : « Aujourd’hui, si vous entendez {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} voix, \v 8 ne laissez pas vos cœurs devenir durs, comme l’a fait le peuple quand il s’est rebellé. C’était le jour où ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont mis à l’épreuve dans le désert. \v 9 Là, vos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont mis à l’épreuve, et ils ont vu ce que j’ai fait \v 10 pendant quarante ans. Alors j’ai été en colère contre cette génération. J’ai dit : “Leur cœur s’égare toujours. Ils n’ont jamais appris à connaître {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} voies.”

decisions.reason: Verses 7-11 quote the Greek of Psalm 95. Where the Hebrew names the places Meribah ("quarreling") and Massah ("testing") (Exodus 17:1-7; Numbers 20:1-13), the Greek translates the names as "the rebellion" and "the testing". The psalm joins the forty years to God's anger; Hebrews, adding "therefore", joins them to "they saw my works", though in 3:17 the author also speaks of God being angry for forty years. Where the Greek psalm says "that generation", Hebrews has "this generation".

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit speaks the psalm now, to the readers
decisions.reason: The author introduces the psalm as what the Holy Spirit says, in the present tense (also 10:15; compare 9:8). The psalm's "Today" becomes the readers' own day (3:13; 4:7).

decisions.choice: the rebellion; the testing: the Greek names for Meribah and Massah
decisions.reason: παραπικρασμός means embittering or provoking, and stands for the place where Israel quarreled with God; πειρασμός is the testing at Massah, where they asked, "Is the LORD among us or not?" (Exodus 17:7).

decisions.choice: harden your hearts: refuse, stubbornly, to listen and obey
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures the heart is the seat of thought and will; a hardened heart will not hear God (Exodus 8:15; Psalm 95:8).

decisions.choice: tested me by putting me to the proof: they demanded that God prove himself
decisions.reason: Hebrews has no object for "tested"; the speaker, God, is the one tested. "In examination" says how: they put God on trial, though they had seen his works for forty years.

decisions.choice: they have not known my ways: they never learned God's ways by experience and followed them
decisions.reason: Knowing God's ways is more than having heard of them; it means walking in them (Psalm 103:7). The picture of a people wandering in heart matches their wandering in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: Today
decisions.reason: The psalm's "Today" is kept as the same word at every level, because the author builds on it in 3:13, 3:15 and 4:7.

decisions.choice: tested me
decisions.reason: Hebrews leaves out the object of "tested"; English needs it. Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}
decisions.reason: Israel's forebears, men and women; the traditional wording is the alternative.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun on mi, mis and the object pronoun me; none on the reflexive "me enojé"
alternatives: no span on the unstressed me
decisions.reason: When God speaks in the psalm, the possessives ("mi", "mis") and the object pronoun "me" refer to him and take the setting, as "my" and "me" do in English. In "me enojé" (I was angry) the pronoun only marks the verb as reflexive and stands for no English word, so it stays plain, like "I" in English.

decisions.choice: [me] pusieron a prueba y [me] examinaron
decisions.reason: Literal turns "in examination" into a second verb so that the supplied pronoun stays a separate word that can carry the setting; joined to a gerund it could not be capitalised. The meaning is the same: they demanded that God prove himself (m5).

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} padres (L); {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} {{gender:antepasados|padres}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the English, Literal keeps "padres" and Balanced and Readable offer "antepasados" (the generation of the exodus, men and women) with "padres" as the traditional form. "Hoy" opens the quotation at every level; the same Spanish wording of Psalm 95 is repeated in 3:15, 4:3, 4:5 and 4:7.

decisions.choice: Leo; msiishupaze mioyo yenu (L, B), msiifanye mioyo yenu kuwa migumu (R)
decisions.reason: "Leo" (Today) opens the quotation, as in the English, and the psalm keeps the same Swahili wording at every level each time Hebrews repeats it (3:15; 4:3, 4:5, 4:7). "kushupaza" is to make stiff and stubborn, the picture behind the idiom (m4); the same verb returns in 3:13 ("asishupazwe"). Readable says it more plainly, "make your hearts hard".

decisions.choice: mababa zenu (L); mababu zenu (B, R); no gender span
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "mababa" (fathers); Balanced and Readable say "mababu" (ancestors), which the English gives through its gender setting. Swahili "mababu" is the ordinary word for the forebears of a people, and the Literal already shows the Greek "fathers", so Swahili has no gender span here.

decisions.choice: Aujourd’hui; la rébellion; the same French wording of Psalm 95 at each repeat (3:15; 4:3, 4:5, 4:7); God’s words in the passé composé
alternatives: the passé simple for the psalm’s past tenses
decisions.reason: The author builds on the psalm’s "Today" and repeats its lines, so each level quotes them in the same French every time, as the English does. "la rébellion" keeps the link with "se rebeller" in 3:16. God is speaking, so his past tenses are in the passé composé ("j’ai été irrité", "j’ai juré"), as French speech is.

decisions.choice: [{{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}]ont mis à l’épreuve (L); {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont mis à l’épreuve (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no object for "tested"; French needs one, and since God is speaking it is a deity pronoun. Literal brackets it. "mettre à l’épreuve" is the book-wide French for this verb (2:18; 4:15).

decisions.choice: they will never enter: a solemn oath
alternatives: if they enter my rest (a question or an unfinished condition)
decisions.reason: The words read "if they will enter". This is the Hebrew form of an oath with the curse left unspoken ("may this or that happen to me if they enter"), so it is a firm denial: they will never enter.

decisions.choice: my rest: God's own rest, which he gives his people to share
decisions.reason: In Psalm 95 "my rest" is first the land God gave Israel as a place of rest (Deuteronomy 12:9-10). In chapter 4 the author shows that it is God's own rest, which began when he finished creating (4:3-4) and is still open (4:9). The same word "rest" is kept through 3:11-4:11 so that the argument can be followed.

decisions.choice: so I swore: the oath follows from God's anger
decisions.reason: ὡς here gives the result ("so that", "accordingly"), as in the psalm.

decisions.choice: They will not / will never enter
decisions.reason: Every level gives the sense of the oath; the literal gloss shows its form.

decisions.choice: rest
decisions.reason: "Rest" at every level, for this word throughout 3:11-4:11.

decisions.choice: No entrarán (L); Jamás entrarán (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek keeps the Hebrew form of an oath, "if they will enter", which means a solemn "they will not" (m1). A Spanish "si" alone would not be understood that way; Balanced and Readable strengthen it to "jamás", as the English says "never".

decisions.choice: reposo
decisions.reason: "Reposo" is the settled word for God's rest through Hebrews 3-4, with "reposo sabático" in 4:9 and the verb "reposar" in 4:4 and 4:10. "Descanso" can sound like a short break from work, less than the rest God himself enjoys and shares (m2).

decisions.choice: pumziko (rest)
decisions.reason: "pumziko" is a rest from work, and it is the word for God's rest throughout Hebrews 3-4, so that 4:4 (God rested on the seventh day, "alipumzika") and 4:9 ("pumziko la Sabato") are heard as the same word. "raha" now usually means comfort or enjoyment, which would lose that link. "ghadhabu" (wrath) at Literal and Balanced, the plainer "hasira" at Readable.

decisions.choice: Ils n’entreront pas (L); Jamais ils n’entreront (B, R); repos at every level
decisions.reason: Every level gives the sense of the oath (m1), as the English does; the Hebrew form "if they enter" would read as a threat left hanging in French. "repos" is kept at every level through 3:11-4:11 so that the argument can be followed.

source.text: βλέπετε, ἀδελφοί, μήποτε ἔσται ἔν τινι ὑμῶν καρδία πονηρὰ ἀπιστίας ἐν τῷ ἀποστῆναι ἀπὸ θεοῦ ζῶντος, ἀλλὰ παρακαλεῖτε ἑαυτοὺς καθ’ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν, ἄχρις οὗ τὸ Σήμερον καλεῖται, ἵνα μὴ σκληρυνθῇ τις ἐξ ὑμῶν ἀπάτῃ τῆς ἁμαρτίας·

records.literal_gloss: Watch, brothers, lest will be in anyone of you heart evil of unbelief in the to fall away from God living, \v 13 but encourage yourselves each day, until which the Today is called, so that not be hardened anyone of you by deceit of the sin;

en.L: Watch out, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in falling away from [the] living God, \v 13 but encourage one another each day, as long as it is called "Today," so that not any of you be hardened by [the] deceit of sin;
en.B: Watch out, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, so that none of you has a wicked heart that refuses to believe and turns away from the living God. \v 13 Instead, encourage one another day by day, while there is still a "Today," so that sin does not deceive any of you and make you hard.
en.R: Be careful, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. Make sure none of you has a wicked heart that does not believe, a heart that turns away from the living God. \v 13 Instead, encourage each other every day, as long as it is still "Today." Then sin will not trick any of you and make your heart hard.

fr.L: Prenez garde, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, qu’il n’y ait en aucun de vous un cœur mauvais d’incrédulité, en se détournant du Dieu vivant ; \v 13 mais encouragez-vous les uns les autres chaque jour, aussi longtemps que [ce jour] s’appelle « Aujourd’hui », afin qu’aucun de vous ne soit endurci par [la] tromperie du péché ;
fr.B: Prenez garde, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, qu’aucun de vous n’ait un cœur mauvais qui refuse de croire et se détourne du Dieu vivant. \v 13 Encouragez-vous plutôt les uns les autres jour après jour, tant qu’il existe encore un « Aujourd’hui », afin que le péché ne trompe aucun de vous pour l’endurcir.
fr.R: Faites attention, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}. Veillez à ce qu’aucun de vous n’ait un cœur mauvais qui ne croit pas, un cœur qui se détourne du Dieu vivant. \v 13 Au contraire, encouragez-vous les uns les autres chaque jour, tant que c’est encore « Aujourd’hui ». Ainsi, le péché ne trompera aucun de vous et ne rendra pas son cœur dur.

decisions.choice: an evil heart of unbelief: a heart that will not trust God
decisions.reason: ἀπιστία is the refusal to trust God's word, as with the wilderness generation (3:19). It is called evil because it leads away from God.

decisions.choice: unbelief shows itself in turning away from the living God
decisions.reason: The phrase says what unbelief does: it deserts the God who is alive and acts (9:14; 10:31; 12:22).

decisions.choice: one another
decisions.reason: The reflexive pronoun is used here for "one another", as it often is (compare Colossians 3:13).

decisions.choice: "Today" from Psalm 95:7
decisions.reason: The word of the psalm names the time of opportunity: as long as God's word still says "Today", the call stands open.

decisions.choice: the deceit of sin: sin promises good and misleads
decisions.reason: Sin is pictured as a deceiver that hardens the heart little by little.

decisions.choice: encourage
decisions.reason: παρακαλέω here is urging and strengthening one another to hold on; "encourage" says both.

decisions.choice: so that sin does not deceive any of you and make you hard
alternatives: so that none of you is hardened by the deceit of sin
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make sin the subject of an active verb, which reads more naturally; Literal keeps the passive.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The readers are men and women; the traditional wording is the alternative.

decisions.choice: anímense unos a otros
decisions.reason: The English says "encourage" at every level. "Exhortar" now sounds like preaching from a pulpit; "animarse unos a otros" is the everyday word for believers strengthening each other day by day.

decisions.choice: la tromperie du péché
decisions.reason: "tromperie" says deceit plainly (m5); "séduction" today suggests attraction more than lying.

source.text: μέτοχοι γὰρ τοῦ Χριστοῦ γεγόναμεν, ἐάνπερ τὴν ἀρχὴν τῆς ὑποστάσεως μέχρι τέλους βεβαίαν κατάσχωμεν.

records.literal_gloss: Partakers for of the Christ we have become, if indeed the beginning of the confidence until end firm we hold fast.

en.L: For we have become partakers of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, if indeed we hold the beginning of [our] confidence firm until [the] end.
en.B: For we have become partners of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, provided that we keep the confidence we had at the start firm and steady to the very end.
en.R: We are partners with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. But that is true only if we keep holding firmly, right to the end, to the confidence we had when we first believed.

es.L: Porque hemos llegado a ser partícipes {{christos:del Cristo|del Mesías}}, si de verdad retenemos firme hasta [el] fin el principio de [nuestra] confianza.
es.B: Porque hemos llegado a ser compañeros {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, siempre que mantengamos firme y segura hasta el final la confianza que teníamos al principio.
es.R: Somos compañeros {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}. Pero eso es verdad solo si seguimos aferrados con firmeza, hasta el final, a la confianza que teníamos cuando creímos por primera vez.

fr.L: Car nous sommes devenus participants du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, si du moins nous retenons fermement jusqu’à [la] fin le commencement de [notre] assurance.
fr.B: Car nous sommes devenus les associés du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, pourvu que nous gardions ferme et solide jusqu’au bout l’assurance que nous avions au départ.
fr.R: Nous sommes associés au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. Mais c’est vrai seulement si nous gardons fermement, jusqu’au bout, l’assurance que nous avions quand nous avons commencé à croire.

sw.L: Kwa maana tumekuwa washiriki wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ikiwa kweli tunashikilia mwanzo wa uhakika [wetu] imara hadi mwisho.
sw.B: Kwa maana tumekuwa washirika wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ilimradi tushikilie uhakika tuliokuwa nao mwanzoni, imara na thabiti, hadi mwisho kabisa.
sw.R: Sisi ni washirika wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Lakini hilo ni kweli tu ikiwa tunaendelea kushikilia kwa nguvu, mpaka mwisho kabisa, uhakika tuliokuwa nao tulipoamini mara ya kwanza.

decisions.choice: partners of Christ: sharing in him and with him
decisions.reason: μέτοχος is the word for the king's companions in 1:9 and for the readers as partners in a heavenly calling in 3:1. It can mean sharing in Christ or being his companions; the two belong together.

decisions.choice: confidence: firm assurance
alternatives: the reality (substance) of our new life
decisions.reason: ὑπόστασις means the underlying reality of something in 1:3, but it can also mean firm confidence, as in 2 Corinthians 9:4 and 11:17; here it is what believers must hold firm, alongside the confidence of 3:6. The sense "assurance" in 11:1 is close.

decisions.choice: we have become partners, and hold on to the end
decisions.reason: The perfect "we have become" speaks of a share already given; the condition says that it is shown to be real by holding firm to the end (3:6).

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (Literal); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: partners
decisions.reason: As in 3:1.

decisions.choice: the confidence we had when we first believed
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the beginning" as the confidence the readers had at first.

decisions.choice: {{christos:del Cristo|del Mesías}} (L); {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: With the title "el Mesías" Spanish contracts "de el" to "del", so the span takes in the preposition. Literal keeps the Greek article ("del Cristo"), as the English Literal keeps "the".

decisions.choice: uhakika (assurance)
decisions.reason: The Greek word here is not the one rendered "ujasiri" (boldness) in 3:6 and 4:16; it is firm, settled assurance (m2), so "uhakika". The English says "confidence" for both.

source.text: ἐν τῷ λέγεσθαι· Σήμερον ἐὰν τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἀκούσητε, Μὴ σκληρύνητε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν ὡς ἐν τῷ παραπικρασμῷ.

records.literal_gloss: In the to be said: Today if the voice of him you hear, not harden the hearts of you as in the rebellion.

en.L: As it is said: "Today, if you hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion."
en.B: As Scripture says: "Today, if you hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, do not harden your hearts as happened in the rebellion."
en.R: Remember what Scripture says: "Today, if you hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, do not make your hearts hard, as the people did when they rebelled."

es.L: Como se dice: «Hoy, si {{plural_you:oyen|oís}} {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voz, no {{plural_you:endurezcan|endurezcáis}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones como en la rebelión».
es.B: Como dice la Escritura: «Hoy, si {{plural_you:oyen|oís}} {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voz, no {{plural_you:endurezcan|endurezcáis}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones como sucedió en la rebelión».
es.R: {{plural_you:Recuerden|Recordad}} lo que dice la Escritura: «Hoy, si {{plural_you:oyen|oís}} {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voz, no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones se vuelvan duros, como hizo el pueblo cuando se rebeló».

fr.L: Comme il est dit : « Aujourd’hui, si vous entendez {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} voix, n’endurcissez pas vos cœurs comme dans la rébellion. »
fr.B: Comme le dit l’Écriture : « Aujourd’hui, si vous entendez {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} voix, n’endurcissez pas vos cœurs comme ce fut le cas lors de la rébellion. »
fr.R: Souvenez-vous de ce que dit l’Écriture : « Aujourd’hui, si vous entendez {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} voix, ne laissez pas vos cœurs devenir durs, comme l’a fait le peuple quand il s’est rebellé. »

sw.L: Kama inavyosemwa: "Leo, mkiisikia sauti {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, msiishupaze mioyo yenu kama katika uasi."
sw.B: Kama Maandiko yasemavyo: "Leo, mkiisikia sauti {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, msiishupaze mioyo yenu kama ilivyotokea wakati wa uasi."
sw.R: Kumbukeni Maandiko yanavyosema: "Leo, mkiisikia sauti {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, msiifanye mioyo yenu kuwa migumu, kama watu walivyofanya walipoasi."

decisions.choice: as it is said: the quotation backs up the call to hold firm in 3:13-14
alternatives: it introduces the questions of 3:16 ("When it says ..., who were they who heard?")
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends the sentence after the quotation, so the phrase goes with the quotation and with what comes before it: hold on while it is said "Today". It could also begin the argument of 3:16-19.

decisions.choice: Psalm 95:7-8 (94:7-8 Greek)
decisions.reason: The opening of the psalm quoted in 3:7-8 is repeated.

decisions.choice: Scripture
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject left implicit in the Greek.

decisions.choice: the Spanish words of 3:7-8, unchanged
decisions.reason: The writer quotes the same lines of Psalm 95 again, so each level repeats its own Spanish wording of 3:7-8 word for word, as the English does, and the reader can see it is the same text.

en.B: Who were the people who heard and yet rebelled?
en.R: Who heard God's voice and still rebelled?

es.B: ¿Quiénes fueron los que oyeron y aun así se rebelaron?
es.R: ¿Quiénes oyeron la voz de Dios y aun así se rebelaron?

fr.L: Car qui, ayant entendu, s’est rebellé ?
fr.B: Qui sont ceux qui ont entendu et se sont pourtant rebellés ?
fr.R: Qui a entendu la voix de Dieu et s’est quand même rebellé ?

sw.L: Kwa maana ni akina nani ambao, baada ya kusikia, waliasi?
sw.B: Ni akina nani waliosikia na bado wakaasi?
sw.R: Ni akina nani walioisikia sauti ya Mungu na bado wakaasi?

decisions.choice: a question: who were they?
alternatives: a statement: some heard and rebelled (though not all)
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts have no accents, and the same letters can be read as "who?" or "some". The SBLGNT reads a question, which fits the series of questions in 3:16-18. Read as a statement, the verse would say that some rebelled but not all who came out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: rebelled: provoked God by defying him
decisions.reason: The verb belongs with "the rebellion" of 3:8 and 3:15.

decisions.choice: heard God's voice
decisions.reason: Readable says what they heard, from the psalm (3:7).

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level ("s’est rebellé", "ont vu")
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Chapters 3-4 are the author’s argument, not narration, so the past events he recalls are in the passé composé at every level, as French uses it in speech and argument. The passé simple is kept for the narrative quoted from Genesis 2:2 in 4:4 (Literal and Balanced).

source.text: ἀλλ’ οὐ πάντες οἱ ἐξελθόντες ἐξ Αἰγύπτου διὰ Μωϋσέως;

records.literal_gloss: But not all the [ones] having come out of Egypt through Moses?

en.L: But [was it] not all those who came out of Egypt through Moses?
en.B: Was it not every one of those who came out of Egypt with Moses as their leader?
en.R: It was the whole people that came out of Egypt with Moses, was it not?

es.L: ¿Pero no [fueron] todos los que salieron de Egipto por medio de Moisés?
es.B: ¿No fueron todos los que salieron de Egipto con Moisés como guía?
es.R: Fue todo el pueblo que salió de Egipto con Moisés, ¿no es así?

fr.L: Mais [n’est-ce] pas tous ceux qui sont sortis d’Égypte par Moïse ?
fr.B: N’est-ce pas tous ceux qui étaient sortis d’Égypte sous la conduite de Moïse ?
fr.R: C’était le peuple tout entier, sorti d’Égypte avec Moïse, n’est-ce pas ?

sw.L: Lakini je, [hawakuwa] wote waliotoka Misri kupitia Musa?
sw.B: Je, hawakuwa wale wote waliotoka Misri, Musa akiwa kiongozi wao?
sw.R: Walikuwa ni watu wote waliotoka Misri pamoja na Musa, sivyo?

decisions.choice: all who came out of Egypt: the whole generation of the exodus
decisions.reason: The people who had been rescued from Egypt were the ones who rebelled. Only Joshua and Caleb of the adults were excepted (Numbers 14:30).

decisions.choice: through Moses: by Moses as God's agent
decisions.reason: God brought them out; Moses led them.

decisions.choice: with Moses as their leader
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "through Moses" means.

records.literal_gloss: With whom and was he angry forty years?

en.L: And with whom was {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} angry forty years?
en.B: And who was it that God was angry with for forty years?
en.R: And who made God angry for forty years?

es.L: ¿Y con quiénes se enojó cuarenta años?
es.B: ¿Y con quiénes estuvo Dios enojado durante cuarenta años?
es.R: ¿Y quiénes hicieron enojar a Dios durante cuarenta años?

fr.L: Et contre qui a-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} été irrité quarante ans ?
fr.B: Et qui sont ceux contre qui Dieu a été irrité pendant quarante ans ?
fr.R: Et qui a mis Dieu en colère pendant quarante ans ?

sw.L: Na ni akina nani aliowakasirikia miaka arobaini?
sw.B: Na ni akina nani ambao Mungu aliwakasirikia kwa miaka arobaini?
sw.R: Na ni akina nani waliomkasirisha Mungu kwa miaka arobaini?

decisions.choice: God's anger for forty years, as in Psalm 95:10
decisions.reason: Here the author joins the forty years to God's anger, as the psalm itself does (compare 3:9-10).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: The subject is God, the speaker of the psalm.

decisions.choice: se enojó, with no subject pronoun
decisions.reason: The Greek verb carries its subject, and so does the Spanish one. Adding "él" only to carry the setting would make it emphatic, so Spanish has no span where the English has "he" (here and in 3:18, 4:3-4, 4:7-8). Balanced and Readable name God, as the English does.

source.text: οὐχὶ τοῖς ἁμαρτήσασιν, ὧν τὰ κῶλα ἔπεσεν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ;

records.literal_gloss: Not with the [ones] having sinned, of whom the limbs fell in the wilderness?

en.L: [Was it] not with those who sinned, whose corpses fell in the wilderness?
en.B: Was it not the people who had sinned, and whose corpses lay fallen in the wilderness?
en.R: It was the people who sinned, was it not? They died, and their bodies lay in the wilderness.

es.L: ¿No [fue] con los que pecaron, cuyos cadáveres cayeron en el desierto?
es.B: ¿No fue con los que habían pecado, y cuyos cadáveres quedaron tendidos en el desierto?
es.R: Fue con los que pecaron, ¿no es así? Murieron, y sus cuerpos quedaron en el desierto.

fr.L: [N’est-ce] pas contre ceux qui avaient péché, dont les cadavres sont tombés dans le désert ?
fr.B: N’est-ce pas contre ceux qui avaient péché, et dont les cadavres sont restés étendus dans le désert ?
fr.R: C’était contre ceux qui avaient péché, n’est-ce pas ? Ils sont morts, et leurs corps sont restés dans le désert.

sw.L: Je, [hakuwakasirikia] wale waliotenda dhambi, ambao maiti zao zilianguka jangwani?
sw.B: Je, hawakuwa wale watu waliotenda dhambi, ambao maiti zao zililala jangwani?
sw.R: Walikuwa ni watu waliotenda dhambi, sivyo? Walikufa, na miili yao ikabaki jangwani.

decisions.reason: The Greek of Numbers 14:29 and 14:32 says that their κῶλον (limbs, that is, dead bodies) would fall in the wilderness. The author uses the same words.

decisions.choice: corpses; bodies
decisions.reason: The word means limbs, and by extension dead bodies; the gloss shows the form.

source.text: τίσιν δὲ ὤμοσεν μὴ εἰσελεύσεσθαι εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν αὐτοῦ εἰ μὴ τοῖς ἀπειθήσασιν;

records.literal_gloss: To whom and he swore not to enter into the rest of him if not to the [ones] having disobeyed?

en.L: And to whom did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swear that they would not enter into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rest, if not to those who disobeyed?
en.B: And who did God swear would never enter {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rest, if not those who refused to obey?
en.R: And when God swore that some people would never enter {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rest, who was {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} talking about? It was those who would not obey.

es.L: ¿Y a quiénes juró que no entrarían en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} reposo, sino a los que desobedecieron?
es.B: ¿Y de quiénes juró Dios que jamás entrarían en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} reposo, sino de los que se negaron a obedecer?
es.R: Y cuando Dios juró que algunos jamás entrarían en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} reposo, ¿de quiénes estaba hablando? De los que no quisieron obedecer.

fr.L: Et à qui a-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} juré qu’ils n’entreraient pas dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} repos, sinon à ceux qui avaient désobéi ?
fr.B: Et qui sont ceux dont Dieu a juré qu’ils n’entreraient jamais dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} repos, sinon ceux qui avaient refusé d’obéir ?
fr.R: Et quand Dieu a juré que certains n’entreraient jamais dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} repos, de qui parlait-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ? De ceux qui n’avaient pas voulu obéir.

sw.L: Na aliwaapia akina nani kwamba hawataingia katika pumziko {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, ikiwa si wale ambao hawakutii?
sw.B: Na ni akina nani ambao Mungu aliapa kwamba hawataingia kamwe katika pumziko {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, ikiwa si wale waliokataa kutii?
sw.R: Mungu alipoapa kwamba watu fulani hawataingia kamwe katika pumziko {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, alikuwa akiwazungumzia akina nani? Ni wale ambao hawakutaka kutii.

decisions.choice: disobeyed: refused to obey
decisions.reason: ἀπειθέω is refusal to obey. In 3:19 the same people are said to have failed through unbelief; for the author the two go together (4:6, 4:11).
God's oath that the generation would not enter the land.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: The subject is God.

decisions.choice: a question and an answer
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long question so that it can be followed.

source.text: καὶ βλέπομεν ὅτι οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν εἰσελθεῖν δι’ ἀπιστίαν.

records.literal_gloss: And we see that not they were able to enter because of unbelief.

en.L: And we see that they were not able to enter because of unbelief.
en.B: So we see that it was unbelief that kept them from entering.
en.R: So we can see why they could not go in: they did not believe God.

es.L: Y vemos que no pudieron entrar a causa de [la] incredulidad.
es.B: Así vemos que fue la incredulidad lo que les impidió entrar.
es.R: Así podemos ver por qué no pudieron entrar: no le creyeron a Dios.

fr.L: Et nous voyons qu’ils n’ont pas pu entrer à cause de [l’]incrédulité.
fr.B: Nous voyons donc que c’est l’incrédulité qui les a empêchés d’entrer.
fr.R: Nous voyons donc pourquoi ils n’ont pas pu entrer : ils n’ont pas cru Dieu.

sw.L: Nasi tunaona kwamba hawakuweza kuingia kwa sababu ya kutoamini.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo tunaona kwamba kutoamini ndiko kulikowazuia wasiingie.
sw.R: Basi tunaweza kuona kwa nini hawakuweza kuingia: hawakumwamini Mungu.

decisions.choice: unbelief: refusing to trust God's promise
decisions.reason: God asked of that generation, "How long will they not believe in me?" (Numbers 14:11). Their failure to enter came from not trusting him.

decisions.choice: it was unbelief that kept them from entering
alternatives: they were not able to enter because of unbelief
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the stress where the Greek does, on the last word, unbelief.
